**JPMorgan blocks outside AI agents from accessing customer accounts**

*The decision to shut out third-party AI agents while building proprietary agentic connections frames an emerging tension between open banking principles and banks' desire to control the AI access layer.*

JPMorgan Chase has blocked external AI agents from accessing customer account data, citing security and customer protection concerns. The bank said it supports authorised data sharing through regulated open banking providers but drew a distinction between those channels and the newer wave of AI agents seeking direct account access.

The bank signalled it is not opposed to agentic connections in principle but intends to enable them on its own terms. The distinction matters: JPMorgan is positioning itself as a gatekeeper rather than a participant in an open ecosystem of AI-initiated financial interactions. For a bank of its scale, the stance is likely to influence how other large institutions approach the question.

The move arrives as the agentic payments space accelerates rapidly. Visa, Mastercard, Stripe and others have launched or joined agentic payment programmes in recent months, and the Euro Banking Association has mapped agentic AI's role in open finance. JPMorgan's position suggests that while banks may welcome AI-driven payments and data sharing, they intend to set the terms on which those interactions occur, rather than ceding control to third-party AI platforms.

*Sources: [JPMorgan blocks outside AI agents from customer accounts Q3 2026](https://qz.com/jpmorgan-blocking-outside-ai-agents-customer-accounts-101326) — Quartz*

**BCG forecasts European payment revenues will reach $408bn by 2030**

*Transactional activity and instant payments are the primary drivers in a projection that underlines Europe's position as a high-growth payments market despite fragmentation concerns.*

Boston Consulting Group has forecast that payment revenues across Europe will reach 408 billion dollars by 2030, with transactional activity and the continued expansion of instant payments identified as the principal growth drivers.

The projection arrives at a moment when Europe's payments landscape is being reshaped by multiple concurrent forces: the SEPA instant payments mandate, the expansion of Wero across new markets, the digital euro's progression through the European Parliament, and intensifying competition between domestic schemes and global card networks. BCG's figure provides a revenue-side anchor for these structural shifts, suggesting that for all the policy complexity, the underlying commercial opportunity continues to expand.

For banks, processors and fintechs operating in European payments, the forecast reinforces the strategic rationale for investment in instant payment infrastructure and account-to-account rails. Whether that revenue accrues primarily to incumbents or to newer entrants will depend in large part on how the regulatory and competitive dynamics of the next four years play out.

*Sources: [BCG forecasts 408 billion in payments in Europe in 2030](https://www.democrata.es/en/economy/the-european-payment-business-will-reach-nearly-408-billion-dollars-in-2030-according-to-boston-consulting-group/amp/) — Demócrata*

**UK Finance calls for global regulatory reform ahead of 2027 G20 presidency**

*Britain's forthcoming G20 presidency offers a window to reshape international financial standards, with open finance and regulatory agility among the priorities identified by the trade body.*

UK Finance has called on the UK government to use its 2027 G20 presidency to push for reform of global financial regulatory standards. The trade body's proposals span open finance, regulatory agility and the broader shift toward data-driven financial services, framing the G20 chairmanship as a rare opportunity to shape international norms.

The intervention comes as the UK is simultaneously consulting on modernising its domestic payments regulation and developing its own open finance framework under Financial Conduct Authority oversight. UK Finance's argument is that domestic and international reform should be pursued in parallel, with the G20 providing a platform to export UK approaches to data sharing and adaptive regulation.

The EU is advancing PSD3 and the digital euro, the US has rewritten its open banking rule under the CFPB, and jurisdictions from Brazil to Switzerland are extending open finance into new sectors. UK Finance sees the current moment as a competitive one for regulatory frameworks, not just for payments products, and is positioning the G20 presidency as the venue to press that advantage.

*Sources: [UK Finance Urges Global Regulatory Reform Ahead of 2027 G20 Presidency](https://ffnews.com/news/uk-has-unique-chance-to-lead-reform-of-global-financial-standards-ahead-of-g20-p-69920a09) — FF News*
